lessons.title: Identifying Common Cabbage Pests
lessons.body: Cabbage is attacked by several pests that can reduce your harvest by half or more if you don't act early. The most damaging are caterpillars: diamondback moth (DBM), cabbage looper, and cabbage white butterfly. DBM larvae are small (1-2 cm), light green, and wriggle violently when touched. They eat small holes in leaves, often from the underside. Cabbage loopers are larger (3-4 cm), green with white stripes, and move by looping. They chew large irregular holes. Cabbage white butterfly larvae are velvety green and also chew big holes. Another major pest is aphids: tiny (1-3 mm), soft-bodied, green or grey, clustering on new shoots and leaf undersides. They suck sap, causing curled leaves and transmitting viruses. You'll also see whiteflies (1-2 mm, white, fly up when disturbed) and thrips (slender, 1-2 mm, cause silvery streaks). Cutworms (3-4 cm, greasy grey) cut seedlings at ground level at night. Flea beetles (2-3 mm, shiny black) make small shot-holes in young leaves. To scout, check 10 random plants per field twice a week. Look on leaf undersides, in the growing point, and on the soil around stems. Use a hand lens (10x) for small pests. Record what you find. Early detection means you can use less pesticide and save money.

lessons.title: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Principles
lessons.body: IPM means using many methods together to keep pests below damaging levels, not trying to kill every insect. It saves money, protects your health, and keeps beneficial insects alive. The steps are: prevention, monitoring, and intervention only when needed. First, prevent pests: rotate cropsâdon't plant cabbage where you grew cabbage, broccoli, or kale in the last 2 years. Use certified seed and resistant varieties like 'Copenhagen Market' or 'Green Challenger' if available. Space plants 45-60 cm apart to improve airflow. Control weeds because they host pests. Use row covers (fine mesh netting) over young plants to block butterflies and aphids. Second, monitor: scout your field twice a week. Check 10 plants per field. Count pests and note which ones. Set action thresholds: for DBM, treat if you find 2 or more small larvae per plant; for aphids, treat if 20% of plants have colonies. Third, intervene: start with the least harmful methods. Handpick caterpillars and drop them in soapy water. Spray a strong jet of water to knock off aphids. Use biological sprays like Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) for caterpillars, or neem oil for aphids and whiteflies. Only use chemical pesticides as a last resort, and choose ones that are less toxic to bees and natural enemies. Always follow label instructions. Rotate chemicals with different modes of action to prevent resistance. IPM is not about doing nothingâit's about doing the right thing at the right time.

lessons.title: Biological Control of Cabbage Pests
lessons.body: Biological control uses living organismsâpredators, parasites, and pathogensâto reduce pests. It's cheap, safe, and sustainable. For cabbage, the most important natural enemies are: parasitic wasps (tiny, 1-2 mm) that lay eggs inside DBM and aphids; ladybird beetles (both adults and larvae) that eat aphids; hoverfly larvae that eat aphids; and spiders and ground beetles that eat cutworms. You can buy some of these, but in Africa it's often easier to conserve what you already have. To encourage natural enemies: avoid broad-spectrum insecticides like lambda-cyhalothrin, which kill everything. Plant flowering plants near your cabbageâe.g., marigolds, sunflowers, coriander, and sweet alyssumâto provide nectar and pollen for adult parasitic wasps and hoverflies. Provide shelter with hedgerows or mulch. You can also apply biological sprays. Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a bacterium that kills caterpillars when they eat treated leaves. It comes as a powder or liquid; mix 1-2 grams per litre of water and spray in the evening. It only works on caterpillars, not aphids. For aphids and whiteflies, use neem oil (azadirachtin): mix 5 ml per litre of water with a few drops of soap, spray every 7-10 days. Beauveria bassiana is a fungus that infects aphids, whiteflies, and thrips; mix 2-5 grams per litre and spray. Always spray in the evening to avoid killing bees and to prevent sunlight from degrading the product. Reapply after rain. Biological control works best when started early, before pest numbers explode.

lessons.title: Common Cabbage Diseases and Symptoms
lessons.body: Cabbage gets several diseases that can wipe out your crop. Learn to recognise them early. Black rot: caused by bacteria. Leaves turn yellow in V-shaped patterns from the edges, then turn brown and dry. The veins turn black. It spreads in wet weather and enters through wounds. Clubroot: a soil-borne fungus. Plants wilt in the day and recover at night. Roots swell into ugly clubs. It survives in soil for up to 20 years. Downy mildew: fungus-like. Yellow patches on upper leaf surface, white fluffy growth on the underside. Spreads in cool, wet weather. Alternaria leaf spot: fungus. Brown spots with concentric rings (like a target) on older leaves. Spreads by wind and rain. Blackleg: fungus. Stem base turns black and shrivels; plants collapse. Powdery mildew: fungus. White powdery patches on leaves, usually in dry, warm weather. Fusarium wilt: fungus. Leaves yellow and wilt on one side; stem inside turns brown. To identify, look at: where symptoms start (old or new leaves), pattern (spots, blights, wilts), and signs (fluff, powder, black veins). Use a hand lens. If unsure, take a photo and ask an extension officer. Prevention is key: rotate crops, use resistant varieties, don't work in wet fields, remove infected plants immediately, and disinfect tools. Once a plant is severely diseased, pull it out and burn itâdo not compost.

lessons.title: Fungicides and Bactericides Application
lessons.body: When diseases threaten your cabbage, you may need to spray fungicides or bactericides. But they only work if used correctly. First, identify the diseaseâfungicides don't kill bacteria, and bactericides don't kill fungi. For fungal diseases like downy mildew, alternaria, or powdery mildew, use fungicides. Common active ingredients in Africa: mancozeb (e.g., Dithane M-45), chlorothalonil (e.g., Bravo), copper hydroxide (e.g., Kocide), and metalaxyl (e.g., Ridomil). For bacterial diseases like black rot, use copper-based bactericides (copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride) or a mix of copper and mancozeb. Always read the label: check dose, safety, and pre-harvest interval (PHI). For example, mancozeb PHI is 7 days; copper PHI is 1-2 days. Mix only what you need. Use clean water. Wear protective clothing: gloves, boots, mask, and long sleeves. Spray in the early morning or late evening when it's cool and calm. Cover both sides of leaves, especially undersides. Use a knapsack sprayer with a fine nozzle. Spray every 7-14 days depending on disease pressure and rain. Rotate chemicals with different modes of action to prevent resistanceâdon't use the same product all season. For example, alternate mancozeb with copper. Never spray when it's about to rain. Store chemicals in a locked cabinet away from food and children. Triple-rinse empty containers and puncture them. Never reuse containers. Dispose of them safely. Remember: fungicides and bactericides are tools, not cures. Use them with IPM.

lessons.title: Preventive Measures and Sanitation
lessons.body: The best way to manage pests and diseases is to prevent them from starting. Sanitation is your first line of defence. Start with clean land: remove all crop debris from previous crops. Burn or bury infected plant materialâdo not compost it. Clean your tools: wash shovels, hoes, and pruning shears with soapy water and then disinfect with 10% bleach solution (1 part bleach to 9 parts water) between fields. Use certified disease-free seed. If saving your own seed, only take from healthy plants. Treat seeds before planting: soak in hot water at 50Â°C for 20 minutes, then cool in cold water. This kills black rot bacteria. Practice crop rotation: don't plant cabbage or its relatives (broccoli, cauliflower, kale, turnip) in the same spot for at least 2 years. Use raised beds or ridges to improve drainageâmost diseases need wet soil. Water at the base of plants, not on leaves. Use drip irrigation or a watering can. If using overhead irrigation, water early in the day so leaves dry before night. Mulch with straw or plastic to prevent soil splash onto leaves. Control weeds because they host pests and diseases. Remove volunteer cabbage plants. Space plants correctly (45-60 cm) for airflow. Stake or prune lower leaves that touch the ground. Inspect your field twice a week. Remove and destroy any plant with disease symptoms immediately. If you see just a few pests, handpick them. Keep a clean field borderâmow grass and remove rubbish. Finally, keep records: note when pests appear, what you sprayed, and the results. This helps you plan better next season. Good sanitation costs little but saves a lot.

quiz.q: Which pest is small, light green, and wriggles violently when touched?
quiz.explanation: Diamondback moth larvae are small, light green, and wriggle violently when disturbed.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for cabbage plants to improve airflow?
quiz.explanation: Spacing cabbage 45-60 cm apart improves airflow and reduces disease.

quiz.q: Which of these is a biological control agent for caterpillars?
quiz.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a bacterium that kills caterpillars.

quiz.q: What is the action threshold for diamondback moth larvae?
options: B) 2 or more larvae per plant
quiz.explanation: Treat when you find 2 or more small DBM larvae per plant.

quiz.q: Which disease causes V-shaped yellow patches on leaves and black veins?
quiz.explanation: Black rot causes V-shaped yellow lesions and black veins.

quiz.q: What is the pre-harvest interval (PHI) for mancozeb?
quiz.explanation: Mancozeb has a 7-day pre-harvest interval.

quiz.q: How should you treat seeds to kill black rot bacteria?
options: A) Soak in hot water at 50Â°C for 20 minutes
B) Soak in bleach for 1 hour
quiz.explanation: Hot water treatment at 50Â°C for 20 minutes kills black rot bacteria on seeds.

quiz.q: Which pest cuts seedlings at ground level at night?
quiz.explanation: Cutworms cut seedlings at ground level during the night.

quiz.q: What is the first step in Integrated Pest Management?
quiz.explanation: IPM starts with prevention to avoid pest problems.

quiz.q: Which natural enemy eats aphids?
quiz.explanation: Ladybird beetles (both adults and larvae) are predators of aphids.

quiz.q: What is the correct mixing rate for neem oil to control aphids?
quiz.explanation: Mix 5 ml of neem oil per litre of water with a few drops of soap.

quiz.q: Which disease causes roots to swell into clubs?
quiz.explanation: Clubroot causes swollen, club-like roots.

quiz.q: When should you spray biological pesticides like Bt?
quiz.explanation: Spray in the evening to avoid sunlight degradation and protect bees.

quiz.q: Which fungicide is effective against downy mildew?
quiz.explanation: Mancozeb, copper hydroxide, and metalaxyl are all used for downy mildew.

quiz.q: How often should you scout your cabbage field?
quiz.explanation: Scout at least twice a week to detect pests early.

quiz.q: What is the correct bleach solution for disinfecting tools?
options: A) 1 part bleach to 9 parts water
B) 1 part bleach to 1 part water
C) 1 part bleach to 99 parts water
quiz.explanation: Use a 10% bleach solution (1:9 bleach to water) to disinfect tools.

quiz.q: Which pest causes silvery streaks on leaves?
quiz.explanation: Thrips feed by sucking sap, causing silvery streaks.

quiz.q: What is the main symptom of clubroot?
quiz.explanation: Clubroot causes swollen, club-like roots.

quiz.q: Which of these is a bacterial disease?
quiz.explanation: Black rot is caused by bacteria.

quiz.q: How long should you rotate away from cabbage and its relatives?
quiz.explanation: Rotate away from cabbage and relatives for at least 2 years.

quiz.q: Which beneficial insect is a parasitic wasp?
options: C) Tiny wasp that lays eggs in DBM
quiz.explanation: Parasitic wasps lay eggs inside pests like DBM.

quiz.q: What is the PHI for copper-based fungicides?
quiz.explanation: Copper fungicides typically have a 1-2 day pre-harvest interval.

quiz.q: What should you do with diseased plant material?
quiz.explanation: Burn or bury diseased plants to prevent spread.

quiz.q: Which pest is tiny, white, and flies up when disturbed?
quiz.explanation: Whiteflies are tiny, white, and fly up when plants are disturbed.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to apply fungicides?
options: A) Spray only upper leaf surface
B) Spray both sides of leaves
quiz.explanation: Cover both sides of leaves, especially undersides, for effective control.

quiz.q: Which disease causes white powdery patches on leaves?
quiz.explanation: Powdery mildew causes white powdery patches on leaves.

quiz.q: What is the recommended dose of Bt powder per litre of water?
quiz.explanation: Mix 1-2 grams of Bt powder per litre of water.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid broad-spectrum insecticides?
quiz.explanation: Broad-spectrum insecticides kill beneficial insects as well as pests.

quiz.q: Which practice helps prevent soil splash onto leaves?
quiz.explanation: Mulching with straw or plastic prevents soil splash and reduces disease.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do when you see a few caterpillars on cabbage?
quiz.explanation: Handpicking caterpillars is a simple, effective first step.
